parameters.Features: Overcurrent Protection;Short-Circuit  Protection;Overvoltage clamping protection;Under-voltage lockout;Thermal Protection;Overload protection

provenance.pins: datasheet p.4 Pin Configuration, TPS16630 PWP (HTSSOP-20) top view

designVerdict: SELECTED as U10/U11, one per channel. 60 V / 6 A eFuse with an integrated FET.
notes: REPLACED an LM5069 (C52940995) driving a discrete NSS085N100S. The LM5069 needs 8 V to operate, so the LED output was dead below a 12 V contract and dead on a laptop port. This part works from 4.5 V, which was the requirement that moved it: running one module from the same cable that flashes the board.

67 V absolute, 75 V for a 10 ms transient at 25 C. Against the SMAJ36CA's 58.1 V clamp that is 1.15x - more margin than the TPS54360B and SS36 on the same node, which sit at 1.03x and are now the binding parts.

DESIGN VALUES, per channel: R_ILIM 3.24 kOhm (5.56 A, from the datasheet's 3k->6A / 4.02k->4.5A table, i.e. I*R ~ 18 kOhm.A), C_dVdT 220 nF, UVLO/OVP string 723k/249k/27.4k (UVLO 4.34 V, OVP 43.8 V against 1.2 V references), C_IN 100 nF, SHDN 100 kOhm pull-down, PGOOD 10 kOhm pull-up shared.

THE dV/dt GAIN IS CALIBRATED, NOT QUOTED. Section 10.2.2.3's worked example - C_dVdT 22 nF gives 300 mA into 100 uF at 50 V - implies the output slew is 33x the dVdT pin's own 2 uA/C slew. At 220 nF that is 300 V/s, so inrush is C_OUT x dV/dt = 0.99 A and the ramp is 120 ms. Verify the gain against the datasheet's Equations 1 and 2 before committing the netlist.

CONSTANT INRUSH IS THE REAL WIN. Under dV/dt control the charging current does not vary with bus voltage or ramp progress, so both channels can be released together (1.98 A against a 5 A contract) and the staggering the LM5069 design required is gone. Ramp time is also independent of load capacitance - 120 ms at 10 or 20 modules - which removes the 12.7-modules-per-channel start-up ceiling the LM5069's fault timer imposed.

RAMPING 3.3 mF IS CHARACTERISED, NOT INFERRED. TI publishes the part powering into 15 mF (Figure 16, Thermal Regulation Loop Response During Power up with Large Capacitive Load) and it regulates its own junction temperature during start-up. This is the question that cost four review rounds on the discrete P-FET.

COST: 31 mOhm integrated against 9.5 mOhm discrete plus a 10 mOhm shunt, so 0.53 W for the pair against 0.28 W, and 1.7 mA IQ each. Thermal headroom falls from 1.29x to 1.19x. The PowerPAD must be soldered to a pour with vias - it is the thermal path the regulation loop depends on.

VARIANT CHOICE: TPS16632 adds adjustable output power limiting but fixes the overvoltage clamp at 39 V, which is under this bus's 37.8 V maximum plus margin. The -30 with adjustable OVP cut-off is the right one here.
MODE pin selects latch-off versus auto-retry and is NOT yet decided - recorded as open in the README.
IMON gives a per-channel current monitor, which is exactly what the shared low-side shunt cannot provide. Unused because there are no spare ADC pins; worth revisiting if the GPIO budget loosens.
